purpose: Editorial seed library only. This is not a systematic review, clinical approval or patient-specific medical guidance.

sources.title: Treatment and Outcomes of Cervical Artery Dissection in Adults: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
sources.inspection: Indexed abstract and official AHA summary inspected; full statement not appraised.
sources.use: Primary clinical framework for explaining care and preparing questions.
sources.limits: A scientific statement is not a personalised treatment plan. Verify exact passages before publishing individual claims.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: ESO guideline for the management of extracranial and intracranial artery dissection
sources.inspection: Indexed guideline excerpts and bibliographic record inspected; direct full-text access challenged by host.
sources.use: Separate extracranial and intracranial dissection; distinguish evidence-based recommendations from consensus.
sources.limits: Do not generalise recommendations across anatomical groups or haemorrhagic and ischaemic presentations.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Vascular Disease Patient Information Page: Cervical artery dissection (CeAD)
sources.inspection: Publisher metadata and indexed patient-information passages inspected.
sources.use: Candidate accessible introductory link and editorial reference for plain-language explanations.
sources.limits: An older educational source; check clinical details against current guidance. Link rather than reproduce.

sources.title: Quality of life in survivors after cervical artery dissection
sources.inspection: Full PubMed abstract inspected.
sources.use: Supports including people with local or transient symptoms and people without significant functional disability.
sources.limits: Older observational cohort; does not establish current population prevalence or show that this app improves outcomes.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Long-term mental health and quality of life in patients after cervical artery dissection
sources.inspection: Publication date and full PubMed abstract inspected.
sources.use: Supports making emotional wellbeing and fatigue visible alongside physical recovery.
sources.limits: Exploratory follow-up of 89 selected patients with excellent early outcomes; not representative prevalence, a diagnostic tool, or an intervention trial.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Information needs of people who have suffered a stroke or TIA and their preferred approaches of receiving health information: A scoping review
sources.inspection: Full open-access article inspected; the review included 36 articles published from 1993 through 2023.
sources.use: Supports short, timely, patient-centred information and attention to rehabilitation, life changes, support options and the differing needs of patients and carers.
sources.limits: The review concerns stroke/TIA, not cervical artery dissection specifically; it searched only German- and English-language literature through June 2023 and did not assess the quality of included studies.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Information provision for stroke survivors and their carers
sources.inspection: Cochrane evidence summary and conclusions inspected.
sources.use: Supports considering active, discussed information with opportunities to revisit and clarify, rather than relying only on passive reading.
sources.limits: The review found uncertain or small effects for several outcomes, particularly for carers; it does not demonstrate that this app improves health outcomes.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Non-pharmacological interventions for caregivers of stroke survivors
sources.inspection: Cochrane evidence summary and conclusions inspected.
sources.use: Supports acknowledging carers’ own support needs and avoiding promises that one programme will work for everyone.
sources.limits: Eight heterogeneous studies involving 1007 participants; the review could not pool results and evidence for the most promising intervention came from one small study. Stroke-specific, not dissection-specific.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Antithrombotic Treatment for Cervical Artery Dissection: A Systematic Review and Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis
sources.inspection: Indexed abstract and key findings inspected; direct full-text access challenged by host.
sources.use: Background for explaining why treatment decisions need individual clinical discussion.
sources.limits: Two trials, 444 patients; the primary composite comparison was not statistically significant. Do not equate non-significance with equivalence or select treatment for a user.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Antithrombotic treatment of cervical artery dissection: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.inspection: Bibliographic search result and abstract excerpt only.
sources.use: Newer candidate to appraise alongside the 2024 randomised-trial analysis.
sources.limits: Study selection, designs and endpoints require full appraisal; publication recency alone does not make a review stronger.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Recurrence of cervical artery dissection: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.inspection: Indexed abstract and methods excerpts inspected; direct full-text access challenged by host.
sources.use: Background for a carefully contextualised explanation of recurrence research.
sources.limits: Extracranial populations; recurrent dissection and subsequent stroke are different outcomes. No individual risk calculator or decontextualised percentage.
sources.rights: Link and original bibliographic annotation only; source content is not relicensed.

sources.title: Cervical Artery Dissection and Sports

sources.title: Stroke Symptoms and Warning Signs
sources.inspection: Official full patient page inspected on 13 October 2026, including B.E. F.A.S.T., other signs, early treatment and symptoms that stop.
sources.use: Source for originally worded B.E. F.A.S.T. explanations and prompt emergency action, including when symptoms stop.
sources.limits: US emergency instructions require localisation. A warning-sign list cannot exclude stroke or replace urgent assessment.
sources.rights: Link and original paraphrases only; source content and artwork are not relicensed.

sources.title: Symptoms of a stroke
sources.inspection: Full official page inspected on 13 October 2026. Displayed review date: 12 September 2024; next review due: 12 September 2027.
sources.use: Supports emergency action for possible stroke, including when signs stop, and distinguishing urgent action from routine appointments.
sources.limits: UK patient information, not dissection-specific guidance. Its UK emergency number is not used in this international preview; symptom lists cannot exclude stroke.
sources.rights: Link and original paraphrases only; source content and artwork are not relicensed.

sources.title: From Fatigue to Energy: Information for patients
sources.inspection: Oxford University Hospitals patient information PDF inspected; page 8 describes spoon theory and attributes it to Christine Miserandino. The leaflet is about neuromyelitis optica, not cervical artery dissection or stroke.
sources.use: Contextual link for an optional metaphor that some people use to talk about limited energy.
sources.limits: This metaphor is not a clinical measure or evidence about fatigue after cervical artery dissection or stroke; the source leaflet addresses another condition and its medical guidance must not be generalized.
sources.rights: Link and original brief paraphrase only; no text or translations from the source leaflet are reproduced.
